What Is a Varactor Diode? Simple Definition and Symbol

A varactor diode (also called a varicap or tuning diode) is a PN junction diode designed to work in reverse bias as a voltage controlled capacitor. When reverse voltage increases, the depletion region widens and the junction capacitance falls. When reverse voltage decreases, the capacitance rises.

Its symbol is a normal diode symbol with a capacitor plate drawn at the cathode side, showing that it is used for capacitance, not for rectification.

PointVaractor diodeNormal rectifier diode
Bias usedReverse bias onlyMainly forward bias
Main jobVariable capacitanceRectify AC to DC
Key ratingCapacitance ratio and Q factorForward current and PIV
Typical useVCO, FM tuning, PLLPower supplies

Because almost no current flows in reverse bias, a varactor diode tunes a circuit with very little power, which is why it replaced mechanical tuning capacitors in radio and TV tuners.
